evidence.ai_role: LASSO, Random Forest and SVM-RFE cross-screen transcriptomic candidate genes to prioritize hub targets for subsequent animal pathway tests.
evidence.tested: Rat injury and pathway-marker assays, sham electroacupuncture comparison and exogenous TRAIL reversal after model-assisted gene prioritization.
evidence.unknown: Acute animal model, no demonstrated human benefit or long-term protection; no gene knockdown or conditional knockout validation.

organization: The Affiliated Hospital of Panzhihua University

source_review.scope: Primary manuscript Methods, relevant Results, limitations and first-version publication metadata reviewed.

summary: LASSO, Random Forest and SVM feature selection prioritized five hub genes, including TNFSF10/TRAIL, from cross-species stroke and electroacupuncture transcriptomic analyses. In an acute rat ischemia-reperfusion study, electroacupuncture reduced injury and apoptosis/inflammation markers; added TRAIL reversed the reported protective effects, supporting involvement of the TRAIL/DR4/DR5 pathway. This preprint concerns a three-day animal experiment, with no human efficacy or long-term outcome evidence. The rescue experiment supports pathway involvement but does not replace targeted genetic validation.
title: Machine learning nominates a stroke pathway tested in rats
